previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted after an outside hospital reported a positive blood culture with gram-positive cocci. Repeat cultures were negative, and the initial result was deemed a contaminant. She presented with worsening lower extremity edema due to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, following a self-reduction of her diuretic regimen. She was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned back to Bumex 4 mg twice daily. Her cough, attributed to viral bronchitis, improved with continued azithromycin and a prednisone taper. Phenytoin levels were subtherapeutic, prompting a dose increase to 900 mg daily after a brief seizure-like episode. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, improved fluid status, and plans for outpatient lab monitoring of phenytoin, INR, and electrolytes.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with cellulitis requiring IV vancomycin
thearpy. Midline  placed by ___ RN, but advancement could not be completed on
the floor.

COMPARISON:  PIC line placement ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ resident) and Dr. ___
(interventional radiology attending) performed the procedure. The attending,
Dr. ___ was present and supervising throughout the procedure.

ANESTHESIA: 1% lidocaine was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues
overlying the access site.

MEDICATIONS: None.

CONTRAST: 2 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 3 min and 48 seconds, 51 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Single lumen PICC placement through the left brachial vein.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

The existing PICC line was extravascular ( confirmed with contrast injection )
and was removed .

Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the patent and compressible left
brachial vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after
intravenous access, which confirmed vein patency.

A peel-away sheath was then placed over a guidewire. The guidewire was then
advanced into the superior vena cava using fluoroscopic guidance. A single
lumen PIC line measuring 54 cm in length was then placed through the peel-away
sheath with its tip positioned in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.
Position of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the
chest. The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. The accessed vein was patent and compressible.

2. Left brachial vein approach single lumen PIC line with tip in the distal
SVC.

IMPRESSION: 

The existing midline access placed on the floor was extravascular and removed.
A new access was placed.

Successful placement of a 54 cm left brachial approach single lumen PIC line
with tip in the distal SVC.

The line is ready to use.
